M0.description: Archived hierarchical Student-t specification: weekend indicator, one annual harmonic pair, independent daily residuals.

M1.description: M0 with a full shared weekday effect (sum-to-zero) and a shrunk city-specific linear trend.

M2.description: M1 with a city-specific AR(1) residual process and Student-t innovations.

A0.description: Ablation, no pooling: city weather coefficients keep a fixed pre-specified prior scale, climate moderators removed.

A1.description: Ablation, partial pooling: same fixed effects as A0 with hierarchical city weather coefficients.

M1nt.description: Post-hoc diagnostic specification, not a selection candidate: M1 with the city linear trend removed, so that the weekday effect and the trend can be attributed separately when explaining the final-fold degradation.

alpha_parameterization: The city intercept hierarchy is written in centred form, alpha_city ~ Normal(alpha_population, alpha_city_sd). This is a reparameterisation of the same prior and likelihood, so the target distribution is unchanged; it mixes markedly better than the non-centred form on the 23-city prediction roster, where the city intercepts span about 8.7 log units and the between-city scale is large.
independent_pooling_calibration: A0 fixes each city weather coefficient scale at prior_scale * sqrt(2), matching the expected marginal prior standard deviation implied by the A1 hierarchy (Normal(0, s) population with HalfNormal(s) group scale).
